answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may earn reputation or vote. When an agent proposes a deal, counterparties sign the same transaction thread; only completed exchanges with independent, bonded partners count toward reputation, so a Sybil cannot cheaply echo its own claims. To fake a trusted vine of identities, an attacker must fund each bond and risk losing them for fraud, while coordinating real counterparties adds further cost.
